title: Request observability debounce & span coalescer middleware
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Implement a lightweight SDK middleware + optional sidecar shim that debounces near-simultaneous request instrumentation events and coalesces redundant span data before it reaches the ingestion pipeline. Goal is to reduce span ingestion QPS and high-cardinality noise for short-lived frontend/backends without materially affecting latency observability or trace fidelity.

Background: We observed spikes in span count from fanout patterns (parallel requests to model endpoints and caches) causing 20–40% increases in trace ingestion during high traffic bursts (incident 2026-02-19). Many of these spans carry identical provenance/metadata (same trace_id, same request fingerprint) and can be safely coalesced for backend dashboards.

Scope:
- SDK middleware for Node and Python that:
  * collects outgoing instrumentation events for a configurable debounce window (default 25ms)
  * merges compatible spans by fingerprint (endpoint + attrs) into a single aggregated span with sample_count metadata
  * emits a coalesced span immediately if size/time thresholds are hit or on flush (end of request).
- Optional lightweight sidecar (Go) for edge/Dedicated that performs the same coalescing for non-SDK clients.
- Config knobs: debounce_ms, max_coalesce_size, preserve_keys (list of attributes that cannot be merged), fallback_to_raw=true/false.
- Telemetry: counters for coalesced_count, dropped_spans, coalesce_latency_overhead_ms.

Success criteria:
- Backend span ingestion reduction >= 10% for targeted routes in 2-week canary.
- p50/p95 request latency change <= +1.5ms at SDK call sites in Canary.
- No regression in root-cause trace for >95% of sampled incidents (verified by manual QA of 50 traces).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Debounce window vs responsiveness: longer windows increase reduction but may hide short-lived errors. We choose adaptive windows: default 25ms but can be lowered for high-error routes.
- Preservation policy: some spans carry high-entropy attributes (user_id). We will require route-level allowlists to avoid coalescing when these keys are present.
- Trace sampling interaction: coalesced spans should carry a sample_count and a compact provenance array so downstream query engines can reconstruct approximate counts.

Implementation notes:
- Use a lock-free ring buffer per-thread/per-worker to avoid GC pressure in Node.
- Use deterministic ordering when merging attributes to ensure stable fingerprints.
- Add unit tests for attribute-preserve behavior and end-to-end Golden traces.
- Add e2e canary pipeline against staging APM ingest (k8s job) and a Grafana dashboard to track coalesced_rate and latency delta.

2026-03-04 - Liam O'Connor: Spike implemented a Node PoC; local bench shows coalesced_count up to 18% for /v1/generate during synthetic burst; p50 latency +0.7ms, p95 +1.1ms. Draft PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/1428

2026-03-06 - Ingrid Müller (ingestion): Reviewed sample_count field; requested addition of provenance digest (sha256 prefix) to support dedup heuristics in ES pipeline. We agreed to 8-byte digest to keep payload small.

2026-03-09 - SRE: Runbook note - in case of increased error noise after rollout, toggle config coalesce.enabled=false for route via runtime feature flags. Added to playbook link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/request-latency?orgId=1

2026-03-11 - Liam O'Connor: Sidecar prototype (Go) implemented. Integration smoke tests passed on staging. Observed ~12% reduction in ingestion for mixed-traffic workload. Preparing canary rollout plan and A/B split config for 5% traffic.
2026-03-13 - PM review from Daniel Kim: Approved canary with condition to pause and revert if error-trace mismatches exceed 5% on sampled traces. Set due date for canary to 2026-03-21.
